title: Carry the request id into the pool's tasks

blocks.text: Request handlers in the order service hand background work to `RequestPool`, and every log line the service writes is tagged with `RequestPool.REQUEST_ID`, the id of the request the current thread is serving. Lines written by pool tasks come out with no request id at all, so nobody can follow an order from its handler into the work it started. Handlers submit both `Callable`s and `Runnable`s, and housekeeping jobs, which serve no request, use `execute(...)`. When the pool and its queue are full, the handler's own thread runs the task, and carries on serving its request afterwards.

Finish `RequestPool` in `src/main/java/practice/RequestPool.java` so that every task a handler submits logs under that handler's request id, and nothing else logs under it: not the housekeeping that runs on the same thread later, and not the handler, which keeps its own id. The handlers' code doesn't change. About fifteen lines in total.

cases.says: a Callable submitted by a handler sees that handler's request id, and one submitted outside any request sees none
a Runnable submitted by a handler sees that handler's request id too
work handed to execute() after a request's task, on the same pool thread, sees no request id
a handler whose thread runs the task itself, because the pool is full, still has its own request id afterwards

origin.section: The GoF Factory Method Is a Creation Hook That Base-Class Code Calls and a Subclass Overrides

concepts: The GoF factory method is an overridable creation method that base-class code calls, so one override changes the product for every caller, and each overload callers reach must be overridden.
